cases.name: Balancing Growth and Risk
cases.description: Model cash flows over time, apply time value of money, connect finance to strategy.

runsheet_segments.focus:
* Welcome everyone to the session
* Introduce the narrative: you are a producer at Fictitious, a streaming platform evaluating three content projects
* Introduce the role, learning objectives, and the three projects on the table
runsheet_segments.notes: Be ready to launch breakouts; if the session is pre-rostered, set up Zoom rooms to match the expected teams. We recommend using pairs for this session, though teams of 3 are okay.

runsheet_segments.focus:
3-MINUTE BREAKOUT: 
Have people join the appropriate team
runsheet_segments.notes: Assist with any Zoom or platform issues.

runsheet_segments.focus:
* Introduce the chapter: "The Numbers Game"
* Brief the teams: review three content projects — their creative briefs and financials
* Highlight the Cash Flow Explorer tool and the goal of forming an initial hypothesis
runsheet_segments.notes: Be ready to launch breakouts

runsheet_segments.focus:
18-MINUTE BREAKOUT: 
* 15 minute timer to play the chapter
* Learners review project briefs (Nomadic Nation, The Shadow Protocol, Silk & Mahogany), explore cash flows, and select which project excites them most
* 3 minutes to review feedback
runsheet_segments.notes: This chapter focuses on raw financials — learners are not yet applying risk-adjusted analysis. Let them form gut reactions.

runsheet_segments.focus:
* Debrief the chapter together
* Ask: Which project caught your eye and why?
* Surface the tension between raw returns (Shadow Protocol) vs. lower risk (Nomadic Nation) vs. balanced (Silk & Mahogany)
   [If falling behind, cut time here to get back on pace.]

* Introduce the chapter: "Building the Case"
* Briefly introduce the concept of risk-adjusted returns and discount rates
* Frame the working session with Haisam (VP of Finance) — he won't hand you answers but will push your thinking
runsheet_segments.notes: Be ready to launch breakouts

runsheet_segments.focus:
23-MINUTE BREAKOUT: 
* 20 minute timer to play the chapter
* Learners use the NPV & IRR Explorer, then have a Socratic conversation with Haisam about discount rates and risk-adjusted analysis
* Learners confirm their final project choice
* 3 minutes to review feedback
runsheet_segments.notes: Key insight: Shadow Protocol's raw numbers look dominant, but its high discount rate (23%) dramatically reduces its risk-adjusted value. Silk & Mahogany has the best NPV per dollar invested.

runsheet_segments.focus:
* Debrief the chapter together
* Ask: How did the risk-adjusted analysis change your view?
* Discuss: Did anyone switch their project choice after applying discount rates?
* Highlight the NPV surprise — Silk & Mahogany's 36.4 cents per dollar vs. Shadow Protocol's 8.6 cents
   [If falling behind, cut time here to get back on pace.]
Short break
runsheet_segments.notes: Put timer on the screen for break

runsheet_segments.focus:
* Introduce the chapter: "The Pitch"
* Remind learners of what Melissa (SVP of Content) evaluates: Financials, Risks, Strategic Value, and Story
* Emphasize: she's evaluating both the project AND the producer
runsheet_segments.notes: Be ready to launch breakouts

runsheet_segments.focus:
23-MINUTE BREAKOUT: 
* 20 minute timer to play the chapter
* Learners use the Pitch Prep Template and Executive Summary tool, then pitch their chosen project to Melissa
* Melissa will push back on assumptions and test conviction
* 3 minutes to review feedback
runsheet_segments.notes: Melissa's feedback includes a narrative outcome (Greenlit / Conditionally Approved / Back to Drawing Board) and a follow-up email. Encourage learners to read both carefully.

runsheet_segments.focus:
* Debrief the chapter together
* Ask: What was hardest about the pitch — the numbers, the risk framing, or the storytelling?
* Discuss: How did Melissa's pushback change your approach?
* Connect to the broader theme: balancing ambition with analytical rigor

* Debrief the overall experience
* Key takeaway: raw financial returns can be misleading without risk adjustment
* Discuss: How does this apply to resource allocation decisions in your own organization?

* Thank everyone for joining
* Distribute survey link
Buffer
